reference.source: Green's Operative Hand Surgery / Campbell's Operative Orthopaedics
clinicalPearls: Characterised by proximal interphalangeal joint hyperextension with distal interphalangeal joint flexion, the reciprocal of a boutonniere deformity

It has several possible origins, including a chronic mallet finger, volar plate laxity at the proximal interphalangeal joint, intrinsic muscle tightness, flexor digitorum superficialis insufficiency, and rheumatoid arthritis
The common final pathway is an extensor imbalance that favours proximal interphalangeal extension and distal interphalangeal flexion
Assessing proximal interphalangeal flexibility with the metacarpophalangeal joint held in different positions helps identify intrinsic tightness (the Bunnell test)
In rheumatoid disease, metacarpophalangeal volar subluxation and intrinsic contracture drive the deformity
The Nalebuff classification grades rheumatoid swan-neck deformity according to proximal interphalangeal flexibility and joint condition
Generic management ranges from figure-of-eight or dorsal-blocking splints for flexible deformities to surgical soft-tissue rebalancing or joint fusion or arthroplasty for severe or arthritic joints
Identifying and treating the underlying cause is essential rather than addressing the posture alone
reference.pathophysiology: Swan-neck deformity reflects an imbalance of the extensor mechanism producing proximal interphalangeal hyperextension and distal interphalangeal flexion. It may begin distally, where a chronic mallet finger allows extensor force to concentrate on the proximal interphalangeal joint and hyperextend it, or at the proximal interphalangeal joint itself through volar plate attenuation, flexor digitorum superficialis insufficiency or intrinsic muscle tightness, with the lateral bands displacing dorsally. It is common in rheumatoid arthritis, where synovitis, metacarpophalangeal joint subluxation and intrinsic contracture combine to create and perpetuate the deformity.
additionalDifferentials: Chronic mallet finger with a secondary swan-neck
Rheumatoid arthritis or other connective tissue disease such as lupus (Jaccoud arthropathy)
Spasticity-related intrinsic tightness, for example in cerebral palsy
Volar plate laxity associated with generalised joint hypermobility
additionalInvestigations: Clinical assessment of proximal interphalangeal flexibility with the metacarpophalangeal joint flexed and extended to detect intrinsic tightness
Plain radiographs to assess joint surfaces, arthritis and subluxation
Examination of the distal interphalangeal joint to identify an underlying mallet
Screening for rheumatoid arthritis or connective tissue disease when the deformity is atraumatic
Application of the Nalebuff classification in rheumatoid cases to guide treatment
redFlags: An underlying inflammatory arthropathy requiring systemic disease-modifying treatment
A rigid, stiff or arthritic proximal interphalangeal joint that limits reconstructive options
Rapidly progressive deformity affecting multiple digits
reference.prognosis: The outlook varies with the cause and the flexibility of the joints; flexible deformities respond well to splinting and soft-tissue procedures, whereas established or arthritic deformities usually require joint surgery and give less predictable results.
pitfalls: Treating the deformity without identifying the primary cause, whether mallet, volar plate or rheumatoid disease
Overlooking intrinsic muscle tightness as a contributor
Ignoring the metacarpophalangeal joint in rheumatoid arthritis
Attempting to splint a rigid joint that will not correct
management: Treat the underlying cause, correcting a chronic mallet finger with distal interphalangeal extension splinting and controlling rheumatoid synovitis with disease-modifying therapy
Manage flexible deformities non-operatively with proximal interphalangeal extension-block splinting (such as figure-of-eight or silver-ring splints) and hand therapy
Release intrinsic tightness and rebalance the extensor mechanism with soft-tissue procedures such as flexor digitorum superficialis tenodesis or lateral band relocation for correctable deformity
Reserve proximal interphalangeal arthrodesis or arthroplasty for fixed or arthritic joints
Address associated metacarpophalangeal subluxation and intrinsic contracture in rheumatoid disease as part of the reconstruction
Use the Nalebuff classification to guide the choice of procedure in rheumatoid cases
Refer to a hand surgery and hand therapy service for assessment and postoperative rehabilitation
